batch: September 4, 2026 - Cadillac injection-well opposition resolution reconciliation
methods: Calculated SHA-256, byte size and page count for the supplied PDF and compared its hash with every published catalog.
Reviewed all five pages from their embedded text and visually verified the first and final pages, including the blank resolution, attendance, vote, adoption and clerk-certification fields.
Reused the byte-identical supplemental-archive record as a cross reference and created no filename-based duplicate.

exactCrossReferences.canonicalName: Cadillac Resolution Opposing Wexford Water Technologies Injection-Well Permit.pdf
exactCrossReferences.finding: The resolution text states that Cadillac had treated Wexford County Landfill leachate for more than 20 years, treated and discharged 14 million gallons in 2016, claimed capacity for up to 20 million gallons annually, and identified cadmium, lead, nickel, chromium, arsenic, benzene, ethylbenzene, ammonia, silver, copper and toluene in the waste stream.
exactCrossReferences.boundary: The supplied form is unsigned and unexecuted: its resolution number, attendance, mover, seconder, vote, adoption date and clerk-certification fields are blank. Separate official Council minutes establish adoption of motion 2017-232. The form contains no PFAS analysis or result, and its general NPDES-compliance language cannot be treated as proof that Cadillac removed PFAS.

queueDecision: No evidence-request item is closed. This exact record was already evaluated and placed in the supplemental archive. It does not supply load-level dates, times and gallons; delivery-linked manifests, invoices, receipts or ledger entries; an executed 2009 agreement or signed successor agreements; the exact final delivery date; synchronized influent, effluent and biosolids sampling; certified 1140 Plett well construction; hydraulic tests; or a site-specific groundwater-flow and source-to-receptor PFAS package.
evidentiaryBoundary: The document preserves proposed resolution text and corroborates Cadillac's historical treatment and capacity claims. It does not by itself prove formal adoption, PFAS removal, delivery-level receiving history, a precise cessation date or a PFAS migration pathway. The separate official minutes remain the adoption record for motion 2017-232.
